inputs.note: Net debt is negative (net cash position of $49.3B). FCF is depressed in FY2025 by ~$91B capex; FY2026 guided capex $180-190B will compress FCF further. DCF models on operating cash flow minus capex trajectory, not on FCF-growth-rate extrapolation, to properly capture the AI infrastructure cycle.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FCF CAGR (0.56% 3yr, 7.81% 5yr) severely understates business growth due to capex surge from ~$32B in FY2021 to ~$91B in FY2025 and guided $180-190B in FY2026. EPS CAGR (34% 3yr) is inflated by FY2025 unrealized equity investment gains. Equity 5yr CAGR (13.3%) is inflated by the $84.75B equity raise in June 2026. Revenue 5yr CAGR (17.2%) is the cleanest anchor for the business's underlying growth trajectory. DCF projects FCF by growing operating cash flow and subtracting an explicit capex trajectory rather than growing last-year FCF.
historical_growth.eps_note: FY2025 net income of $132.2B includes material unrealized equity investment gains; FY2025 EPS is not representative of recurring earnings power. FY2024 EPS of $8.04 (post-split) is cleaner.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: FY2025 equity surged ~$100B due to $84.75B equity raise (June 2026); organic 4yr equity CAGR 2020-2024 is 9.1%.

base.narrative: AI infrastructure build peaks in FY2026-2027 at $185-210B capex, then normalizes as data centers come online. Operating CF grows 25% in Y1-Y2 driven by Cloud acceleration (+63% in Q1 2026) and Search monetization of AI, then decelerates as base effects grow. FCF troughs near breakeven in Y1-Y2 and recovers strongly to $261B by Y5 as capex moderates. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects AI-embedded long-run growth premium over GDP.

bull.narrative: Cloud inflects faster (backlog $462B converts rapidly), Search AI monetization outperforms, Waymo begins meaningful revenue contribution by Y4. CapEx produces higher ROI sooner (Cloud supply constraint eases), driving earlier and larger FCF recovery. WACC lower reflecting GOOGL's exceptional credit quality, $50B net cash, and durable moat. Terminal growth 4% reflects Cloud+AI+Waymo compounding.

bear.narrative: Antitrust remedies (search data-sharing, exclusive deal ban) and AI-driven search displacement materially impair Search revenue growth. Ad tech divestiture strips $30B+ network revenue. Cloud growth disappoints as AWS/Azure defend share. CapEx produces poor returns; FCF negative for Y1-Y3. Higher WACC reflects regulatory and structural risk premium. Terminal growth 2.5% reflects mature advertising business with structural headwinds.

sensitivity.note: Matrix uses Base Case FCF projections across WACC and terminal growth combinations. Rows = WACC (7-11%), Columns = Terminal Growth (2.0-4.0%). Current price $337.39 is above all base-case matrix values, implying the market prices in stronger AI monetization than the base case assumes or a WACC below 7%.

sanity_check.trigger_reason: Current price ($337.39) exceeds base case intrinsic value ($296.94) and all sensitivity matrix values. EV/EBIT at 32.4x is above the historical median of ~22x. The market is pricing in a bull-case or better AI monetization scenario.

market_implied_assumptions.interpretation: The market is effectively capitalizing operating cash flow (adding back capex as value-creating investment) rather than penalizing FCF compression during the investment cycle — a common valuation approach for infrastructure-heavy growth companies during a capex supercycle (analogous to Amazon 2012-2015 during AWS buildout).

embedded_option_value.note: Waymo's $126B Series D valuation ($16B raise, Feb 2026) represents ~$10.29/share of embedded option value not captured in FCF-based DCF. Management expects Waymo to be financially meaningful in 2028+.

sanity_check.assessment: At $337.39, GOOGL is fairly valued to modestly overvalued on a traditional FCF-based DCF basis (base IV $296.94, -12%). However, the stock is near the bull-case entry price ($326.37), which implies the market is pricing in strong AI monetization — consistent with 63% Cloud growth, $462B backlog, and Search queries at all-time highs. The valuation is defensible if: (1) Cloud sustains 40%+ growth through 2027, (2) Search monetizes AI Overviews at historic rates, and (3) CapEx ROI materializes by 2028-2029. Key downside risks are antitrust remedies, CapEx overspend, and search query displacement.

valuation_philosophy.approach: Operating Cash Flow minus Explicit CapEx Trajectory
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Standard FCF-growth-rate extrapolation materially misstates Alphabet's value during the AI infrastructure capex supercycle. FY2025 FCF of $62.4B (after ~$91B capex) and near-zero FY2026 FCF (after $185-190B capex) do not represent normalized earning power. Instead, this model projects operating cash flow growth (reflecting the underlying business acceleration) and subtracts an explicit capex trajectory that peaks in FY2027 and normalizes through FY2030 as AI infrastructure becomes productive. This approach is consistent with how infrastructure-intensive growth companies (Amazon in 2012-2016, AT&T, cable companies) are valued during major investment cycles.
key_assumptions_to_watch: Operating CF growth rate Y1-Y2 (25% base): driven by Cloud 40-63% growth and Search AI monetization — most critical variable
CapEx normalization timeline: if 2028 capex stays elevated at $200B+ rather than declining, FCF recovery delays significantly
Terminal growth rate: 3.5% base assumes AI-embedded long-run growth above GDP; sensitive to AI commercialization success
WACC: 9% base is appropriate for GOOGL's credit quality and net cash; antitrust regulatory risk could justify 10-11%

warning_banner.message: FCF is structurally depressed 2026-2027 by $180-210B annual capex. This DCF models on operating cash flow minus capex trajectory. At $337, the stock prices in a bull-or-better AI monetization scenario — base case fair value is $297 (-12%). The bull case entry price for a 15% CAGR target is $326 (-3% from current).
